The key distinction is that offline eval checks whether your application is working correctly, whereas online eval tells you whether your application is running normally in production. The two are not rivals or replacements—they are complementary and are meant to be used together.

testCases.input: why can't we test llm apps the same way we test normal software?
testCases.expectedOutput: Testing an LLM application is not as straightforward as testing normal software. Traditional software testing checks whether deterministic logic gives the expected output—the same input always produces the same fixed output. LLM application testing is different because the behaviour is probabilistic rather than deterministic, so instead of checking for one fixed correct output, you have to check whether the output meets a definition of 'good'. That is why LLM evaluation needs a different, more involved approach than traditional software testing.

testCases.name: test_case_4
testCases.input: why can't we just compare the generated sql query with the correct one character by character?
testCases.expectedOutput: Comparing the generated SQL query with the correct query character by character is not a good strategy, because a single result can be produced by multiple different queries. The query your data analyst wrote and the query the LLM generated to solve the same problem may be different textually, yet both are correct. So instead of matching the query strings, you run both queries on the database, get a result set—a table—from each, and compare the two tables. If both tables are the same, the generated query is considered correct.
